title: Joshua Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 9.

questions.question: Which peoples' kings gathered together to fight against Joshua and Israel?
options: Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
Philistines, Egyptians, Babylonians, Amorites
Romans, Greeks, Egyptians, Hittites
Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:1 lists these specific peoples as the kings who heard about Joshua's actions and gathered against him.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the kings gathering together?
options: To make peace with Joshua and Israel
To fight with Joshua and Israel
To form a trade alliance
To seek help from Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: To fight with Joshua and Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:2 clearly states that the kings gathered to fight with Joshua and Israel with one accord.

questions.question: From which city did the inhabitants act wily and pretend to be ambassadors?
options: Jericho
Gibeon
Ai
Gilgal
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeon
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:3-4 describe how the inhabitants of Gibeon acted craftily and pretended to be ambassadors.

questions.question: What items did the Gibeonites carry to make their journey seem long?
options: New sacks and fresh wine bottles
Old sacks, old wine bottles, old shoes, and old garments
Weapons and fresh bread
Jewelry and silver coins
questions.correctAnswer: Old sacks, old wine bottles, old shoes, and old garments
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:4-5 describe the Gibeonites carrying old sacks, rent wine bottles, old shoes, and old garments to appear as if they came from a far country.

questions.question: Where did the Gibeonites go to meet Joshua and the men of Israel?
options: Jericho
Gilgal
Ai
Gibeon
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:6 states that the Gibeonites went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal.

questions.question: What did the Gibeonites request from Joshua and the men of Israel?
options: To be made rulers over Israel
To make a league (treaty) with them
To give them land
To join them in battle
questions.correctAnswer: To make a league (treaty) with them
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:6 records the Gibeonites asking for a league with Israel.

questions.question: What was the men of Israel's initial reaction to the Gibeonites' request?
options: They immediately made a league
They doubted if the Gibeonites dwelt among them
They attacked them
They sent them away
questions.correctAnswer: They doubted if the Gibeonites dwelt among them
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:7 shows that the men of Israel questioned if the Gibeonites dwelt among them and how they could make a league.

questions.question: How did the Gibeonites describe themselves to Joshua?
options: Enemies of Israel
Servants of Joshua
Servants of the LORD God of Israel
Kings of a far country
questions.correctAnswer: Servants of the LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:8-9 shows the Gibeonites claiming to be servants of the LORD God of Israel and coming from a far country.

questions.question: True or False: The Gibeonites said they came because they had heard about all the LORD did in Egypt.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:9 states they came because they heard the fame of the LORD and all He did in Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Israel immediately asked counsel of the LORD before making a league with the Gibeonites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14 explains that the men took the victuals and made a league without asking counsel at the mouth of the LORD.

questions.question: Which event happened first according to Joshua 9:1-14?
options: The kings gathered to fight Israel
The Gibeonites came to make a league
Israel heard of the Gibeonites' deception
The men of Israel made a league with the Gibeonites
questions.correctAnswer: The kings gathered to fight Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:1-2 states that the kings gathered first, then the Gibeonites acted to make a league (verses 3-14).

questions.question: True or False: The Gibeonites' bread was fresh and soft when presented to Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:5 states the bread was dry and mouldy, showing it was old.

questions.question: What excuse did the Gibeonites give for their deception when confronted by Joshua?
options: They wanted to live in peace
They were afraid because they heard God commanded Moses to give Israel the land and destroy the inhabitants
They wanted to trick Israel for land
They were forced by other kings
questions.correctAnswer: They were afraid because they heard God commanded Moses to give Israel the land and destroy the inhabitants
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:24 explains the Gibeonites' fear due to hearing how God had commanded Moses to give Israel the land and destroy its inhabitants.

questions.question: What did Joshua and the princes swear to the Gibeonites after making peace?
options: That they would kill them
That they would give them land
That they would let them live
That they would make them kings
questions.correctAnswer: That they would let them live
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:15 states that Joshua made peace and a league to let the Gibeonites live.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Israel were pleased with the princes' decision to honor the oath to the Gibeonites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:18 says the congregation murmured against the princes for keeping the oath.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 9:10, which two kings of the Amorites are mentioned as having been defeated beyond the Jordan?
options: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan
Pharaoh king of Egypt and Sihon king of Heshbon
Og king of Bashan and Jabin king of Hazor
Jabin king of Hazor and Pharaoh king of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:10 specifically mentions the two kings of the Amorites defeated beyond Jordan as Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, which is crucial for understanding Israel's conquest under God's guidance.

questions.question: What reason did the inhabitants of Gibeon give for their deception in Joshua 9:24?
options: They feared the LORD's command to destroy the land and wanted to save their lives
They sought to ally with Israel for protection against other tribes
They wanted to test Israel’s faithfulness to their God
They desired to be servants to Israel willingly
questions.correctAnswer: They feared the LORD's command to destroy the land and wanted to save their lives
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:24 explains that the Gibeonites acted out of fear because they heard that the LORD commanded Moses to give the land to Israel and destroy its inhabitants, so they resorted to deception to preserve their lives.

questions.question: How did Joshua and the men of Israel respond when the Gibeonites asked for a league, according to Joshua 9:7?
options: They questioned if the Gibeonites dwelt among them before making a league
They immediately accepted the Gibeonites as servants
They refused to make any league without consultation with God
They prepared for battle instead of making a league
questions.correctAnswer: They questioned if the Gibeonites dwelt among them before making a league
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:7 shows Israel’s cautious approach by asking the Gibeonites if they lived among them, indicating concern about their identity before agreeing to any covenant.

questions.question: What did Joshua do after the men of Israel took the victuals from the Gibeonites without asking counsel from the LORD, according to Joshua 9:14-15?
options: He made peace and a league with them to let them live
He immediately nullified the agreement upon learning of the deception
He consulted with the priests before deciding
He sent the Gibeonites away without making a league
questions.correctAnswer: He made peace and a league with them to let them live
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14-15 states that the men took the provisions without seeking the LORD’s counsel, and Joshua proceeded to make peace and a league with the Gibeonites, allowing them to live.

questions.question: What does Joshua 9:18 indicate about the reaction of the congregation when the princes swore to the Gibeonites?
options: The congregation murmured against the princes
The congregation rejoiced at the peace made
The congregation was indifferent
The congregation immediately attacked the Gibeonites
questions.correctAnswer: The congregation murmured against the princes
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:18 reports that the people murmured because they were upset that the princes swore an oath to the Gibeonites and spared them from being smitten.

questions.question: According to Joshua 9:20, why did the princes decide to let the Gibeonites live despite the congregation's complaints?
options: To avoid wrath because of the oath sworn to them
Because the Gibeonites showed repentance
Because the LORD commanded mercy
Because the Gibeonites promised to pay tribute
questions.correctAnswer: To avoid wrath because of the oath sworn to them
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:20 explains that the princes chose to keep their oath to avoid incurring God's wrath, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness to promises made in God's name.

questions.question: What role were the Gibeonites assigned after the league, as stated in Joshua 9:21?
options: Hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation
Priests serving at the altar of the LORD
Kings and rulers under Israel's authority
Spies and scouts for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:21 states that the Gibeonites were made hewers of wood and drawers of water, serving the congregation and the altar, which was a way to integrate them under Israelite service without granting full citizenship.

questions.question: According to Joshua 9:12-13, what evidence did the Gibeonites use to convince Israel that they came from a far country?
options: Dry, moldy bread; rent wine bottles; old garments and shoes
New bread; fresh wine; bright garments
Weapons and chariots from a distant land
Letters from other kings endorsing them
questions.correctAnswer: Dry, moldy bread; rent wine bottles; old garments and shoes
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:12-13 describes how the Gibeonites presented dry, moldy bread, rent wine bottles, and old garments and shoes to simulate a long journey and convince Israel they came from afar.

questions.question: What does Joshua 9:16 teach about the timing of the discovery of the Gibeonites' true location?
options: It was found out three days after making the league
It was discovered immediately upon their arrival
It was never discovered during Joshua’s leadership
It was found out after several months of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It was found out three days after making the league
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:16 reveals that after three days from the league, Israel heard that the Gibeonites were actually their neighbors, showing the consequences of not seeking God’s counsel.

questions.question: How does Joshua 9:14-15 illustrate the importance of seeking God’s counsel before making decisions?
options: The men took victuals and made a league without consulting the LORD, leading to deception
The men prayed and received clear guidance before making the league
The men sent spies to verify the Gibeonites’ story first
The men refused to make any agreements without God's explicit command
questions.correctAnswer: The men took victuals and made a league without consulting the LORD, leading to deception
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14-15 highlights that Israel acted without seeking the LORD’s counsel, which resulted in their being deceived by the Gibeonites, teaching the importance of spiritual discernment.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Joshua and the Gibeonites in Joshua 9:22-23 teach about integrity and consequences?
options: Deception led to a curse of servitude despite the league
Joshua immediately released them with no consequences
Joshua ignored their deception and treated them as equals
The Gibeonites were rewarded for their cleverness
questions.correctAnswer: Deception led to a curse of servitude despite the league
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:22-23 shows that although Joshua allowed the Gibeonites to live, their deceit caused them to be cursed to serve as bondmen, teaching that integrity matters and deceit has consequences.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 9:17, the children of Israel came to the cities of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kirjathjearim on the third day after making the league.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:17 states that on the third day after the league, Israel journeyed and came to those cities, confirming the timing and location of their arrival.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 9:19 indicates that the princes advised the congregation to break their oath and attack the Gibeonites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:19 explains that the princes told the congregation they could not touch the Gibeonites because they had sworn by the LORD God of Israel, emphasizing faithfulness to promises.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 9:26 says that Joshua delivered the Gibeonites out of the hand of Israel so they were not slain.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:26 confirms that Joshua spared the Gibeonites from death, honoring the league despite their deception, demonstrating the seriousness of oaths and mercy.

questions.question: Based on Joshua 9:20, what principle can be learned about keeping promises even when circumstances change?
options: Keeping promises prevents wrath and honors God
Promises can be broken if deception is discovered
Promises are conditional and can be disregarded
Promises only matter if made privately
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping promises prevents wrath and honors God
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:20 highlights that the princes chose to keep their oath to avoid God's wrath, teaching the biblical principle of faithfulness and integrity in promise-keeping regardless of changed circumstances.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 9.

questions.question: Why did the princes of Israel decide not to harm the Gibeonites despite being deceived?
options: Because they feared the Gibeonites' army
Because they had sworn an oath by the LORD God of Israel
Because Joshua was sympathetic to their plight
Because the Gibeonites offered a large tribute
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had sworn an oath by the LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:19 shows that the princes reminded the congregation they had sworn an oath by the LORD God of Israel, so they could not touch them without breaking their covenant.

questions.question: What consequence did Joshua pronounce on the Gibeonites after discovering their deception?
options: They were to be killed immediately
They were cursed to be bondmen, hewers of wood, and drawers of water
They were to be exiled from Israelite territory
They were to pay a heavy fine
questions.correctAnswer: They were cursed to be bondmen, hewers of wood, and drawers of water
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:23 states Joshua cursed them so that none would be freed from being bondmen and serving as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God.

questions.question: How did the Gibeonites explain their deception to Joshua?
options: They wanted to avoid slavery
They were commanded by the LORD to deceive Israel
They feared for their lives because they heard of God's command to destroy inhabitants
They sought to take over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They feared for their lives because they heard of God's command to destroy inhabitants
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:24 reveals the Gibeonites said they were afraid because they heard the LORD commanded Moses to give the land to Israel and destroy the inhabitants, so they acted to save their lives.

questions.question: What task were the Gibeonites assigned to serve within the congregation?
options: Priests in the tabernacle
Heavers of wood and drawers of water
Judges over Israelite tribes
Merchants and traders
questions.correctAnswer: Heavers of wood and drawers of water
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:21 and 9:27 show the Gibeonites were made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar of the LORD, serving in that capacity as promised by the princes.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated in Joshua 9 by the Gibeonites' deception and subsequent curse?
options: Chiasmus illustrating reversal of fortunes
Parable teaching moral lessons
Typology foreshadowing New Testament servitude
Alliteration emphasizing deceit
questions.correctAnswer: Typology foreshadowing New Testament servitude
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites’ servitude as hewers of wood and drawers of water (Joshua 9:23, 27) typologically foreshadows the humble service expected in the New Testament (e.g., John 13:14-17), illustrating servant leadership.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of making oaths and their binding nature, as seen in Joshua 9?
options: Numbers 30:2 – Keeping vows made to the LORD
Genesis 1:1 – Creation of the heavens and earth
Exodus 20:3 – The Ten Commandments
Leviticus 19:18 – Love your neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 30:2 – Keeping vows made to the LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:19-20 emphasizes the seriousness of oaths sworn by the LORD God of Israel, paralleling Numbers 30:2, which commands people to keep all vows they make to the LORD, highlighting covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: The Gibeonites claimed they came from a very far country because they had heard what about Israel's God?
options: His miracles in Egypt and victories over Amorite kings
His laws given to Moses on Mount Sinai
His creation of the world
His covenant with Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: His miracles in Egypt and victories over Amorite kings
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:9-10 shows the Gibeonites said they came from afar because they had heard of the fame of the LORD and all He did in Egypt and against the Amorite kings beyond Jordan.

questions.question: What was the condition of the Gibeonites’ provisions when they approached Joshua to make a league?
options: Fresh and plentiful
Dry, mouldy bread and old wine bottles
Spoiled meat and stale water
New garments and shoes
questions.correctAnswer: Dry, mouldy bread and old wine bottles
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:5 and 9:12 describe the Gibeonites’ ruse: they wore old garments, shoes, and carried dry, mouldy bread and old, rent wine bottles to appear as though they had traveled a long distance.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Israel consulted the LORD before making a league with the Gibeonites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14 explicitly states the men took the victuals of the Gibeonites and made a league without asking counsel at the mouth of the LORD, leading to their deception.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua ultimately spared the Gibeonites and made them servants rather than killing them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:26-27 shows that Joshua delivered the Gibeonites out of the hand of Israel and made them hewers of wood and drawers of water, sparing their lives due to the oath sworn.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'hewers of wood and drawers of water' in Joshua 9:21?
options: It signifies priestly duties
It refers to menial servitude and subjugation
It means warriors for the congregation
It implies merchants and traders
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to menial servitude and subjugation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew terms here describe lowly, servile work, indicating the Gibeonites’ cursed servitude status, emphasizing their subjugation to Israel despite being spared (Joshua 9:21).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of solemn oaths and faithfulness found in Joshua 9?
options: Hebrews 6:16-18 – God’s unchanging purpose and oath
Matthew 28:19 – The Great Commission
Romans 12:2 – Transformation by renewing the mind
James 2:14 – Faith without works is dead
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 6:16-18 – God’s unchanging purpose and oath
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:16-18 discusses God’s oath as a guarantee, echoing the seriousness of oaths sworn in Joshua 9:19-20, underscoring the binding nature of divine covenants.

questions.question: What historical and cultural context helps explain the Gibeonites’ fear of the Israelites’ conquest?
options: The Israelites’ recent victories and God’s command to destroy inhabitants
The Gibeonites had previously been allies of Egypt
The Israelites were known for their merciful treaties
The Canaanites were all united in a single kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The Israelites’ recent victories and God’s command to destroy inhabitants
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:24 explains the Gibeonites feared because they heard God commanded Moses to give Israel the land and destroy its inhabitants, reflecting the violent conquest context of the ancient Near East.

questions.question: What does Joshua 9:22 reveal about Joshua’s leadership style when confronting the Gibeonites’ deception?
options: He responded with immediate violence
He openly confronted them with a direct question
He ignored the deception for political reasons
He sought advice from the priests
questions.correctAnswer: He openly confronted them with a direct question
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:22 shows Joshua called the Gibeonites and asked why they beguiled Israel, indicating his direct and confrontational leadership approach to the issue.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament story contains a similar theme of deception to secure peace or safety, as seen in Joshua 9?
options: Genesis 27 – Jacob deceives Isaac to receive blessing
Exodus 14 – The parting of the Red Sea
1 Samuel 17 – David and Goliath
Daniel 6 – Daniel in the lions’ den
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 27 – Jacob deceives Isaac to receive blessing
questions.explanation: Genesis 27 involves Jacob using deception to secure his father’s blessing, paralleling the Gibeonites’ deceptive tactics in Joshua 9 to secure a treaty, showing recurring biblical themes of deception with mixed outcomes.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which groups of people gathered together with one accord to fight against Israel according to Joshua 9:1-2?
options: The Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
The Egyptians and Philistines
The Babylonians and Assyrians
The Moabites and Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: The Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, Jebusite
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:1-2 states that the kings on this side Jordan including the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite gathered themselves to fight with Joshua and Israel.

questions.question: What deceptive strategy did the inhabitants of Gibeon use to make a league with Israel?
options: They pretended to be travelers from a far country by wearing old clothes and carrying moldy bread
They attacked Israel unawares during the night
They sent a secret message to Israel's enemies
They bribed the princes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They pretended to be travelers from a far country by wearing old clothes and carrying moldy bread
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:4-5 recounts that the Gibeonites wore old clothes, carried moldy bread, and wine bottles that appeared old to deceive Israel into thinking they came from a distant land.

questions.question: What was Israel's initial reaction to the Gibeonites' claim of coming from a far country?
options: They doubted and asked how to make a league with them
They immediately accepted their claim without question
They declared war on them
They sought God's counsel before responding
questions.correctAnswer: They doubted and asked how to make a league with them
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:7 shows that the men of Israel questioned the Gibeonites, saying 'Peradventure ye dwell among us; and how shall we make a league with you?' indicating skepticism.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human sin and deception is illustrated by the Gibeonites' actions in Joshua 9?
options: Human beings can resort to cunning and deceit to preserve their lives, reflecting the fallen nature's propensity to sin
Humans are incapable of lying or deceit
Deception is always holy when done for survival
God condones all human actions without exception
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings can resort to cunning and deceit to preserve their lives, reflecting the fallen nature's propensity to sin
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites' use of deception (Joshua 9:3-13) exemplifies the doctrine of human sinfulness and the tendency to use dishonest means even for self-preservation (Genesis 3; Romans 3:23).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is challenged by Israel's failure to seek counsel from the LORD before making the league with the Gibeonites?
options: God's providence and wisdom
God's omnipotence
God's holiness
God's omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence and wisdom
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14 states that the men took the victuals without asking counsel at the mouth of the LORD, showing a failure to rely on God's providence and wisdom in decision-making.

questions.question: What consequence did the Gibeonites face after their deception was discovered?
options: They were cursed to be bondmen, hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God
They were put to death by Israel
They were exiled from the land
They were made kings over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They were cursed to be bondmen, hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:23-27 records that Joshua cursed them and made them servants who would serve as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar of the LORD.

questions.question: How does Joshua 9:15-20 demonstrate the importance of oath-keeping and covenant faithfulness before God?
options: Israel refrained from attacking the Gibeonites because the princes had sworn an oath by the LORD, showing God's covenant demands
Israel ignored the oath and attacked the Gibeonites
Oaths made to foreigners are not binding
God condones breaking oaths when convenient
questions.correctAnswer: Israel refrained from attacking the Gibeonites because the princes had sworn an oath by the LORD, showing God's covenant demands
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:15-20 highlights that despite the deception, Israel could not break the oath sworn by the princes before the LORD, emphasizing the sacredness of covenant vows (Numbers 30:2).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Joshua 9:24-25 and Joshua 9:26 regarding human fear and divine mercy?
options: Human fear of God's judgment leads to deceptive actions, yet God's mercy can preserve life despite sin
God punishes all deception without exception
Fear of man is always a sign of weak faith
Divine mercy is only extended to the faithful Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Human fear of God's judgment leads to deceptive actions, yet God's mercy can preserve life despite sin
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:24-25 shows the Gibeonites acted out of fear of Israel's God, while 9:26 reveals Joshua spared them, demonstrating God's merciful restraint despite their sin.

questions.question: How does the narrative of the Gibeonites fit into the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It illustrates God's sovereign preservation of life and covenant integrity amid human sinfulness
It shows Israel's failure to conquer all enemies
It reveals God's rejection of all Canaanite peoples
It demonstrates the futility of covenant-making
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's sovereign preservation of life and covenant integrity amid human sinfulness
questions.explanation: The Gibeonite story (Joshua 9) fits redemptively by showing God's mercy in preserving a deceiving people and upholding covenant oaths, reflecting themes of grace amid human failure (Genesis 12:3).

questions.question: What does Joshua 9:22-23 reveal about God's justice in relation to human deception within His covenant community?
options: God pronounces a curse restricting the Gibeonites to servitude, indicating justice tempered with mercy
God ignores the deception and rewards the Gibeonites
God annihilates the Gibeonites immediately
God elevates the Gibeonites to leadership roles
questions.correctAnswer: God pronounces a curse restricting the Gibeonites to servitude, indicating justice tempered with mercy
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:22-23 shows that Joshua cursed them so none would be freed from servitude, demonstrating God's justice addressing sin but also sparing their lives.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by the princes' refusal to break their oath despite the Gibeonites' deception?
options: God's faithfulness and holiness
God's wrath and vengeance
God's silence
God's forgetfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and holiness
questions.explanation: The princes' insistence on honoring their oath made before the LORD (Joshua 9:19) reflects God's attribute of faithfulness and the holiness that demands covenant integrity (Psalm 89:34).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Joshua 9 teaches that God condones deception. What does Joshua 9:14-15 and 9:23-27 actually teach about God’s stance on deception and sin?
options: God allows consequences for deception but exercises mercy and enforces covenantal justice
God endorses deception as a good practice
God ignores deception completely
God rewards deception with blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God allows consequences for deception but exercises mercy and enforces covenantal justice
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:14-15 reveals Israel's failure to seek God's counsel, and 9:23-27 shows the Gibeonites cursed to servitude but spared from death, demonstrating that God does not condone deception but shows mercy while upholding justice.

questions.question: What does the episode of the Gibeonites teach about sanctification in the life of Israel as God's covenant people?
options: Sanctification includes maintaining covenant faithfulness and dealing justly with sin among the community
Sanctification means ignoring all sins for unity
Sanctification is only about external rituals
Sanctification excludes making covenants with outsiders
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification includes maintaining covenant faithfulness and dealing justly with sin among the community
questions.explanation: The princes’ oath (Joshua 9:15-20) and Joshua’s judgment (9:22-27) show sanctification involves obedience to God's covenant and just discipline within the community.

questions.question: By synthesizing Joshua 9:6-13 and 9:21-27, what teaching emerges about human responsibility and divine sovereignty in covenant relationships?
options: Humans are responsible for truthfulness in covenants, but God sovereignly enforces justice and mercy when sin occurs
God relinquishes all control over human covenants
Humans bear no responsibility in covenant making
Divine sovereignty invalidates human oaths
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are responsible for truthfulness in covenants, but God sovereignly enforces justice and mercy when sin occurs
questions.explanation: The Gibeonites’ deception (9:6-13) shows human responsibility for honesty, while Joshua’s covenant enforcement and judgment (9:21-27) reveals God’s sovereign role in justice and mercy.

questions.question: What does Joshua 9:17-18 reveal about the tension between human leadership and the people regarding covenant decisions?
options: The congregation murmured against the princes for honoring the oath, showing tension between leadership decisions and popular opinion
The people unanimously supported the princes
The people were unaware of the covenant
The princes acted without any opposition
questions.correctAnswer: The congregation murmured against the princes for honoring the oath, showing tension between leadership decisions and popular opinion
questions.explanation: Joshua 9:18 records that the congregation murmured because Israel did not smite the Gibeonites, indicating tension between leadership’s oath-keeping and the people's desire for immediate justice.
